utterances.text: That night, no, no, I did not have it in my apartment. I returned it that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: To whom did you return it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want the name or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us to whom did you return it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked you, do you want me -- the name or the party?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Both the name and the party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The name would not mean anything to you. His name was Mirso. And I gave him the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the party is the ABiH, I assume?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was with the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And why did you give him the rifle? It was your rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not my rifle. Because I had taken the rifle from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you go home in your uniform or in civilian clothes? Did you have a uniform on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, yes. I went home in the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was that the ABiH uniform or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was a uniform with a Croatian insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. So then you heard this argument that night -- that was the night on the night of the 8th, is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That is a wrong date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where did you make a mistake in date? In this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what date was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The night between the 16th and the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was that April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And then on the 9th, or in the night between the 8th and the 9th, this is when it started, when you heard shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten to 5.00 on the 9th of May, 1993. The first shell that was fired from a hand-held rocket launcher was fired into the living room of the apartment where I slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that also a mistake? You said the balcony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can show it to you. It was the wall separating the balcony from the living room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, my question was, did the shell hit the balcony or the living room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The wall separating the balcony and the living room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher's assistance to give us back the photograph - I don't know exactly the number - so you can show us exactly where the shell impacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: To make things easier, 16.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it's proper to put this photograph on the ELMO because that will identify, in my view, where the witness lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go into the private session, but it cannot be -- no, no, no, you're right. We should go to the private session. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The Juka, is that the name of a man called Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a man named Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he a Bosniak Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He probably is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was that the man who came from Sarajevo as a hero?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How did you know, who told you, that Juka was with the Convicts Battalion? Was this something that you heard in the bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You did not hear that from me, that Juka was in the Convicts Battalion. I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, that was my understanding. When you said that Juka took you from the School of Economics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we saw Zeljko Bosnjak at the School of Economics, in the yard there, a colonel of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. We will get to that right away, to Zeljko Bosnjak, but Juka had nothing to do with the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, but they were together that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, how did you know that Zeljko Bosnjak was with the Convicts Battalion, and that on top of that, he had the rank of colonel, on that 8th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you had really listened to what I was saying, you would remember that I said that later on, I learned that he was a colonel in rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I was asking you about the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about the 8th of May. I left the school of economics on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you did not know who that man was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that he was Zeljko Bosnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that's how you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know his rank. I knew that he was with the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And later on, you heard from people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He personally arrived. He personally came to the swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. We'll get there. We'll get there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. All I want to say, that I learned about it a couple of days later, after the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, who did Misic shoot at? We are now in front of the ministry, as you said, and you came -- and Misic shot at somebody. Who was it that he shot at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, no, no, no, no. Don't read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like not to mention the name. It's not written there. Can I say it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he's an army soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Should we go to private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. It's just for this one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The faculty is down near the Bijeli Brijeg stadium. The ministry is about 700 or 800 metres before that, across from the old Velez stadium, in the direction of Balinovac or the Bakamok [phoen] Street, whichever way you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you were taken to Balinovac? Is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were taken down on to Zujanica Street, and it passes the Velez stadium, which now has all these coffee bars. It intersects the street that goes from the Rondo to the Velez stadium. And then there was the SIS building, a small house, and then past there, to the right, in a -- there is an older building. It used to be the Zagreb Bank before and during the war was a ministry. I don't know what ministries were in there. I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And can you tell me in relation to that building what -- where was the Tobacco Institute or something like that that -- was there something called like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Tobacco Institute is about four kilometres away from that, on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I see that it is 1.00, Your Honours. I will not be long after the break. I will go on with my cross-examination, but I will not take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I just need to find the map of Mostar. I believe it's Exhibit 11.8. It's 11.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, would you please take the pointer and show us on this map this ministry in the former Zagrebica Bank, and then the location of the Tobacco Institute. Please use the pointer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the cemetery -- old Zagreb bank.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness. He is too far from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, Witness, you have to turn on the other mic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Kindly show us the Tobacco Institute in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just for the record, will you please describe the location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Below the Hasan Brkic bridge on the left-hand side. The streets towards Buna and Blagaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And now, please, show us the mechanical engineering school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mechanical engineering school. The university buildings are here. That's the old Dzemal Bijedic University.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the Velez stadium. If you are coming from the direction of Strelcevina, if you are going from Rondo, it's on the right-hand side. If you are coming from Vranica, it's on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you were all taken by Juka's soldiers to the old stadium. Were you personally taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it's the site below the old Partizan bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right, cemetery. Thank you, Witness. Now, tell me, you were arrested and taken away by Juka's soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Juka's and Tuta's soldiers, because both followed us. Some went in front and some behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How do you know they were Tuta's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Djeko Bosnjak is Tuta's man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But at that time you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know he was a colonel. I learned two days later at the swimming pool that he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Now, tell me, when you were arrived outside that building of the ministry, you said Misic, Tuta, and Primorac were already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you give me the names of some people who saw Misic shoot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they come here, you'll have the opportunity to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't remember a single name of a person who eye-witnessed this? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People heard it. I don't know how much they could see because they were in two columns. The moment when he cursed our mothers and said that we had killed his son, that's the moment when he took out his gun and fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You have said this already. I was asking you to tell me some names of people who saw it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only give you the names of people who were present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's the only thing I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that those were people who were there, and I've already listed them today. I can repeat those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we should go into private session because I don't see why anyone who was in the BH army would deserve our going into private session every time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll go to the private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And nobody else fired except this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said [redacted] was hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was hit by a Motorola by Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And no one else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm mentioning names again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, then, Juka came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Juka was already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a minute. Did Juka try to prevent this? Did he scream at Misic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Juka stood in front of Misic and Mr. Tuta, and said that he had promised us outside the school of economics, and this was true, that we would not be killed, that we would not be hurt in any way. And then Tuta said, "Take these people to Siroki Brijeg and execute them."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And Juka's men then took you to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on a bus. Juka's men were with us but without Juka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And as you arrive outside the police station in Siroki Brijeg; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you then turned over to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only after 30 or 40 minutes. The policemen were standing outside and they eventually turned us over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the civilian police, then, took you over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 40 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And from then on, you were taken care of by the police. You were accommodated in those cells, as you said, you were fed, and so on and so forth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 33 of us were placed in two cells --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We heard about that already. I'm only asking you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I'm replying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I was asking you, the police took care of you, put you in cells, fed you, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you believe a 200 gram food -- tinned food enough for six persons --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That was not the question. I was asking you who took you over, who took care of you. Please don't be offended. Tell me, you said today when you went to the swimming pool, you were guarded by home guards. Who were those home guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the swimming pool. At the swimming pool, we were guarded by drivers who drove the trucks carrying the wood that we had chopped and loaded. There were ten of them, about ten of them. And they called themselves "home guards" when we were working on the canal, when we were digging the canal. It was a later occasion when we were guarded by self-styled home guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, you were guarded by drivers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the swimming pool, yes. But not at the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And who guarded you at the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over seven days at the canal, we were guarded by a special unit of civilian police. Several days later, maybe 7, maybe it's 11 days, we were guarded by civilian policemen. And later yet, we were guarded again by the guards who were guarding us at the Tobacco Institute. And after them came civilians who didn't go to the front but who put on uniforms and called themselves "home guards." And they guarded us, they continued guarding us until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, were they armed? I mean the drivers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't hear your answer. Were the drivers armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, this water canal, this water supply canal that you were digging, was it for a village on a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That canal we were digging, we dug it up to the road by which we had come. And from that point on, a bulldozer could continue. The guards told us that it was for Tuta's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the canal and Tuta's house, there were perhaps only two more houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell us kindly, that swimming pool where you worked, was it the town pool?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fifteen years ago maybe, probably. But nowadays, it was Jablanica and those drivers who told us where the restaurant would be, where the tennis grounds would be, the tennis courts, and it was in that direction that we cleared the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And it was supposed to be taken over by Jablanica, you said today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, together with Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just one more question about this swimming pool. Did you also get food only once a day at the swimming pool as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How about cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, unless some of the drivers gave us one. We got on one occasion about ten T-shirts because ours were very soiled. They brought them in a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So let me get this straight. At least one driver had to be present at the swimming pool at all times because they were coming and going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were at the swimming pool all the time, at least six or seven, because they were afraid that we would run.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, if you could follow me, I would like to turn back to that canal when you were carrying explosives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean sewage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, sewage. In the sewage tunnels, were guards also with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you crossed over to the other side where the BH army was. Couldn't you escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could, but out of the 13 of us, four were brought in. The brother of one man had already been killed and they told us that if one of them -- one of us runs, this man's brother would be killed. And we couldn't run, in other words, because that man's brother would die.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, did this explosive go off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let us go back to Siroki now. How tall is the man whom you refer to as Colonel Andabak? Is he like me or like you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he's taller.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is he like me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taller still, not much taller, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Not much. I'm 170. Is he 175 perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, more. He is a very big man, broad-shouldered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, did you ever see him on television before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In October, you said you were released. Did somebody release you privately of their own accord? Did they just say, "You're free to go"? And who was it, if so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mate Boban had intervened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You hadn't mentioned that in your statement or in your testimony before. You said you were released by Tuta's deputy in October.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was after the intervention of Mate Boban that Andabak personally released me, from his office on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what is the connection between these Poskok men and the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Poskok men were in the same prefab house that we were placed in. I said -- I didn't say anything about them being connected with the Convicts Battalion. I only said there existed the Poskok Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Apart from them, was there anyone else at the tobacco station? Were there any other soldiers who were stationed there, spent the nights there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would finish work about 5.00, 5.30, depending on the day --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you, Witness, but if you would be so kind as to follow my question. You give me very extensive answers all the time. I'm supposed to lead you by my question to make this more concise and articulate, but I don't seem to be having much success. I put to you a very simple and clear question. Apart from these Poskok men, were there any other troops stationed at this Tobacco Institute that you know of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not even the Poskok Battalion spent the nights there. The soldiers didn't sleep there. They only came by day. Nobody slept there except for us prisoners. In another part of the Tobacco Institute, I can't say, because we weren't allowed to walk around the perimeter, except a little in front of our building, we were allowed sometimes to stay outside for 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: All right. About these people whom you enumerated, Cikota, Romeo Blazevic, Darko Dodig, and some others, were they from Siroko or did they come from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cikota came from Siroko. I know that because I went to work on his house for about a month with interruptions. Romeo Blazevic came from Mostar. Darko Dodig resides in Mostar. Where he is from originally, I don't know. And who else did you ask about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't know. Those are the names that you mentioned in your answers to my learned friend. I believe there was one Vinko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you mean the waiter. He came from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember that in your statement given to the investigators of this Tribunal, you said that all of them were from Mostar and that they came from Mostar? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, except for Ivan Cikota. Yes. He came from Mostar too. Dolma came from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, if you can. In your statement, you only mentioned the persons whose names I just read to you and you said that they were from Mostar, and now that you mentioned the others that you mentioned, you only saw them in Ljubuski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Isn't there a difference there? Don't you notice that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They also came from Mostar to Ljubuski. All the persons I mentioned who as having come in to beat people, all came from Mostar, instead of Cikota and the others who came late at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, the alleged questioning from -- on the part of the SIS and person you called Andabak, was it not all about why a certain person was released that allegedly this Bosnjak person released him and how much money was given for that? Wasn't it all about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Andabak's questioning was before the SIS and VOS questioning and it was the questioning about some safe and some money, allegedly in a basement in Vranica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well, stop there now for a moment. Do you know that you never mentioned that until now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not mention Andabak?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, never by full name. And you never mentioned that Andabak questioned you about a safe. You nowhere mentioned that at any time. I'll give you a statement so you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I remember. Because I remember I said that on the 78th day, he questioned us. I think that that is record -- that was recorded. I did not mention details in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you tell me, what is the truth here? Did Andabak question you or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 78th day of my arrival on the 10th of May, I was questioned by a colonel who identified himself as Colonel Andabak in a room -- in their office where the guards were guarding us. And those were the guards who were with us at the Tobacco Institute who were there in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. No need to repeat it. You said all that already. So far, you have been telling us that you were guarded by the members of the Convicts Battalion. And a few minutes ago, you told me that you were never guarded by the members of the Convicts Battalion, either at the swimming pool or the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our guards in the prison were members of the -- that is, in the Tobacco Institute --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Hold on. Are you referring to the Tobacco Institute as a camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because it was a camp. That was part of the Tobacco Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Then you said that you slept in the part of the building which was -- where the Siroki Brijeg battalion called Poskok was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Poskok Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And then I asked you what was their connection with the Convicts Battalion, and you said none.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Half of the prefab building was the command post of the Poskok Battalion, and the other part was where we were kept by these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me, if you remember, a name of any of these men.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember Soldo, Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are these first names, last names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are both last names. One had nickname Djaga, and they showed their IDs as belonging to Tuta's unit because they said they had no problems when they were going to Mostar when they showed this ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know you never said until now that this was Tuta's swimming pool, and you never mentioned the name Jablanica before. You never mentioned it anywhere. It is today for the first time that you are doing it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I can give you the statement, and you can perhaps show me where you mention the name of Andabak or Jablanica, or where did you mention that Tuta and he was going to share this half and half. In fact, I can say this, that you said about Andabak: "On the 78th day of my detention, I was beaten by Tuta's deputy, a soldier nicknamed Robija, and another soldier in the compound of the command of the Convicts Battalion." That's all. You never mentioned Jablanica anywhere, nor did you ever mention that it was Tuta's swimming pool, the one in the city. I will give you the statement to look at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave the basic information. I did not go very wide because I would not have finished in four months had I described what I experienced day by day. But I did mention that on the 78th day of my detention, I was questioned, and the man who questioned me identified himself as Colonel Andabak. And when I left house, I also see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I did not want to give you the statement to look, but you did not mention Colonel Andabak in any of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour, because one thing, if the investigator asked this question or not, and if he wrote it down in the witness statement. He was asked today during the examination-in-chief who was in charge, and that's why he gave the name of Jablanica. I don't think that it's an appropriate question from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, when we evaluate all this evidence, of course we will take the live evidence this witness gave today as the first-hand evidence. As for the previous statement, we believe they have only the reference value in this aspect. But the Defence counsel has the right to ask any questions arising from the previous statement. That is a matter for us to decide which evidence will be relied upon. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have only a few more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In your statement, you said expressly that the canal for Tuta's home, and it was for his pool. How do you know that he had a pool in his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please give me the statement because that's not how it was stated. A pool was mentioned, but it was the one over in the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm going to underline it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can ask the usher to please show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I doubt very much whether we should put that statement on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is no secret, and there are no names mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question is: Did you or did you not state this? You said that you never did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you did state it after all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, Your Honours, maybe we should move into the private session, but this name was mentioned in the open session a few days ago, but if you think that it should be mentioned in private, we could. I don't see what the secrecy is about. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because this name was mentioned in the private session in the direct examination, so we should go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. BB, I am Branko Seric, attorney from Zagreb, and I represent Mr. Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have several questions that I would like to ask in private session at the very beginning so that we can then not need to go into the private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. BB, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you were beaten in the prison in Ljubuski and you mentioned -- and my learned friend elicited names of Takac, Pehar, Blazevic, Dodig, from you. When was this in relation to the day when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- on the ninth or tenth day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can we agree this would have been around the 19th, 18th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can I please ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit number D211 or P704 from the Prosecution binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. BB, near the top, you have something that looks like a stamped 00795359. That's a page number that appears to be stamped. This is it. Please look at it. Just keep going. You'll see the number 00795359. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the part that is underlined.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Combat group 4 -- I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. What is under Item 1? What is the name under --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Damjan Peric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Commander, Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How about 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Romeo Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Djuro Djidic, soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you see the name of Vinko Martinovic written anywhere on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please turn to the page which has the last three digits 386.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you see the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vinko Skrobo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And who is under number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what is to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you conclude from this that Martinovic was commander to Blazevic, Peric, and Djidic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But Ernest Takac was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That was not my question. You can give the document back to the usher. Mr. BB, you mentioned some professor, teacher, Krilic. We don't know this person. Did you know this person before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When did you meet him for the first time? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the pool, because he lived in Dobrkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was this at Ljubuski or Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness BB, this is now at page 21, line 9 through 13. You stated that you saw him for the first time in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all, because he could not have been at Ljubuski with another 56 prisoners throughout this period. Until his death, he was at the school in Dobrkovic. That's where civilians from Mostar from imprisoned, the ones that worked with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, could you tell me from which document that page 21, line 9 through 13 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is in today's transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You made a mistake. That's a different professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. You said that was the name. You said Professor Krilic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how we're going to resolve the problem. In the transcript today, on page 21, lines 9 through 13, witness mentioned Professor Krilic in Ljubuski, and that's when they talked for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It seems to me my learned colleague is mistaken. He mentioned some professor from Mostar without giving his name. Krilic is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to Her Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My note says Professor Krilic. My note agrees with Mr. Seric. My note here says somebody was killed with a karate kick in the chest, and my cryptic note has "Professor Krilic" beside it, and then the next question was, Who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It's a different camp. It's Dobrkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Let me see what my note says. At that time, he was talking about Mr. Tuta's house and digging the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It's different. It's different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It's a different occasion --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, it's a different occasion. Ljubuski was somewhere in May, and digging the canal was in July or August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It was in the early part of the evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the transcript says, A professor from Mostar, who was brought just with his socks on his feet, and with his jaw swollen. It does not mention any name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not the occasion when he is describing a professor who was killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That professor was mentioned in context with Stela, but I didn't mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I know that I heard this last name, but I must be mistaken. Tell me, did you know that professor from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Bosnica [phoen] Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Which part of town was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Pijesak or -- it was Pijesak near the first primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to him then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he was brought there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you when he had been arrested, and did you tell anything about the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the fourth day after our arrival on Siroki Brijeg, he was brought with just his socks on, with his jaw swollen to such an extent that the policemen brought him Aspirin for pain. He said, "I was brought from my apartment," and we asked him who had hit him, he said, "Stela and his men." Who he meant by "his men," I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. BB --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: With the passage of time, Witness, does your memory get better or worse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My memory is good, thank God.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: With the passage of time, though, does your concentration deteriorate? Do some details become blurred or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- I'm trying to forget, and some details I managed to edit out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But a few years ago, when you were giving the statement, your memory of these events was better, wasn't it? So why wasn't this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't want my statement to become a novel. I wanted to say the most important things, the essence, to the investigators, and when the trial begins, I thought I would get an opportunity to clarify all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So today we are going to hear the novel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Believe me, if I recounted day for day what happened to me there, it would have been a novel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Don't you think it would be valuable to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's why I came here, to recount everything, day by day, if so required.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But I'm telling you, you didn't mention it in 1997. If your reason is that you didn't want to write a novel then, then that can be the end of my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true. I didn't go into too much detail because the statement would take too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you questioned about Vinko Martinovic, Stela, at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The questions that they asked were answered in the statement. They mentioned twice Stela. They asked me whether I saw him on Siroki Brijeg. I said yes, when I did the paint work and when I cleaned the offices in Tuta's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And even then, you didn't see fit to mention this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because the beating of prisoners was a regular occurrence, and if you mentioned every instance of it, it would take very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So on the 4th and 5th of May -- sorry, 4th and 5th of September, when you were giving the statement, you were also aware of this incident. You were aware of this incident even then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 4th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: 1997, when you were questioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And did you fail to mention it on purpose or you had forgotten it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't forget it because that's impossible to forget, because that professor asked later to be brought shoes, and when he got his Aspirin and his pain killers, we borrowed them from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who was the warden in Ljubuski prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I never set eyes on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That warden, was there a warden at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. We were released four times within three days into the courtyard and we didn't see anyone apart from the couple of guards who were standing there, and the people who had arrived on that particular day. Since I spent there only two nights and three days before I left Ljubuski, I couldn't learn much about it. I didn't see anything but the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that there was no one in control in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I saw, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you ever report the abuse by soldiers, even outsiders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never. I managed to get out of there, to escape outside, and I tried to forget. I tried to forget all that I had gone through. I tried to return to the normal life that I had before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In Siroko, when these persons whom you had mentioned would come in - and we read their names just a minute ago - did they do so of their own accord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were let in by the policemen. The policemen probably had to unlock the doors for them, and they would come in and beat at random, indiscriminately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it? I'm sorry, I don't -- I'm not skipping from one prison to another on purpose, but that's where my questions are taking me. Was there any control over the guards, seeing how people from outside could come in as they pleased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't possibly know if and what kind of control there was because we were locked up constantly. From 9.00 p.m. to 3.00 a.m., people came in dressed in a variety of uniforms. The doors of our cells would be unlocked and we were beaten, which means there was no control over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did it happen on several occasions, on different days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the first night when we were brought to Ljubuski, it happened every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you know, did you know then, or did you find out later, that these soldiers who visited - you said they were not from Mostar - that these soldiers were under anyone's control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. They came in as they pleased and did as they pleased, which means they were under no control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they have a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were they behaving violently in an arbitrary way of their own accord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, they came after 9.00 p.m., most of them after 12.00, and they were under the influence, drunk, which probably means they came straight from various bars. And they came in -- I don't know whether somebody sent them or they came of their own accord. But they did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, based on this, that they were rowdy and drunk, if I can use this term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were, indeed, intoxicated. And judging by their bloodshot eyes, some of them may have been drugged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us from your experience -- I don't know how rich it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very rich.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me from your experience with people if men in such a wild state, prone to violence, under the influence of alcohol and other substances, are possible to control, especially if they are armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They didn't come in with their weapons, with their rifles. And control can be exerted over anyone by anyone who wishes to exert control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can probably agree on that. But there are certain special states, conditions which are difficult to control. That's what I had meant. Did you ever complain about this situation in Ljubuski to the warden, to anyone who could possibly hear out your complaint about such behaviour on the part of people who had nothing to do with the prison at all? Did you ever complain about this wilful violent behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian policemen were present, because they held the keys to our cells. It was them who unlocked the cells in the first place, and they told us, "We are not in a position to help you. We are civilian police. These men here are soldiers in uniforms." They couldn't help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. BB, you mentioned on several occasions the anti-terrorist group, abbreviated as ATG, and you referred to the Mostar ATG, saying that this group was commanded by Vinko Martinovic. Are you aware of the fact that on the territory of Mostar, there were several such ATGs and several commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of Benko Penavic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please show this witness Exhibit 14.19, Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see anything, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll wait. Can you see now? Do you have the photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the demarcation line, that is the Bulevar? Can you point it to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me get this closer. I'll put it back. One cannot see the Bulevar here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you see the Santic Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Yes, I can see the Santic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise in the right quarter of the photograph, this street going across?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's going towards the old hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that street, if you can possibly remember? Doesn't matter. Do you see the Health Centre on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please leave the photograph there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly like to show this witness the Prosecution Exhibit from the 10th volume, P521. Sorry, it's the 11th volume, the 11th binder. Exhibit 521. Be so kind as to read for us the title of this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Command of the 1st battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot follow. We do not have this document. Will you put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please read us parts of the line and show us which part of the line was held by the HVO and tell us what the first paragraph says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The positions are held by members of PS of Mostar." I don't know what "PS" is. "Within the first 12 hours, on the first defence lines, there are 12 policemen plus another 12 policemen in a state of combat readiness, on alert."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That's enough. Now you see the second paragraph, "Old high school"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I have a request. Since from the 10th May onwards, I don't know about the demarcation line because I was on Siroki Brijeg, all I know is that near the third school, there were sacks put up, and I was brought behind the house of Mujaga Komandina through a demolished house up to the high school, and that's where I carried the explosives. As for the defence lines" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sir, allow me to lead me with your questions, and you have just started answering them, but we have to follow a sequence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters repeat that they do not have this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that you couldn't know about this when you were in prison at the time. Below the part of the paragraph which says, "Line, old high school," read for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Positions are held by members of the 1st Battalion of the military police, whereas reserve positions are held by members of the Mostar PS."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Turn the page. You will see a line that says, "Old high school, Health Centre." Read it for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Positions held by 4th -- 3rd Battalion of the HVO Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, read this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Positions are held by Mrmak ATG."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph, we see, "Aleksic House Zahum." Read the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Positions held by the 4th Battalion of the 3rd Brigade of the HVO."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Does it follow from this that the zone of responsibility of Vinko Martinovic is precisely the Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't anywhere near the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to show this witness the drawing 14.2. It's from the first binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness BB, can you orient yourself on this drawing, to show us with a pointer Aleksa Santic Street, one, Bulevar, two, and the Health Centre, three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: High school and Bulevar, Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where would that primary school and the courthouse be located, where you said you set explosives, you laid explosives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here. That's where the primary school is. That's where the courthouse is. This is the primary school. I mean the courthouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Show us where Balinovac is, or Balinovac, whatever the accent is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said today, in your examination-in-chief, that it was from the soldiers themselves that you found out they belonged with Stela's unit, and you said some of them bragged of this fact. Is it possible that they -- some of them simply bragged without really being members of Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anything is possible. But not in regard to Dolma whom I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please, just answer my questions. You said that many, without naming names, many bragged that they belonged to Stela's unit. I'm asking you again: Is it possible that some among these many bragged without really being members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware - and I have a reason for asking this, without going into your background or that of my client - are you aware that Vinko Martinovic joined the Convicts Battalion after the 12th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that it was based on some other circumstances that you belonged in a circle close to Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A circle?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, at Balinovac, I socialised for a long time, for many years, within a certain circle of people among which Vinko Martinovic, Stela, was well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And one last question: Can you remember today who worked together with you on the town swimming pool? If you can remember those names, we might go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the town pool at Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can remember seven or eight names. Because for two days, another team of our people worked there, and I can't remember exactly who I worked with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask, Your Honours, that we go into private session once again so the witness can tell us these names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I apologise, Mr. President, for saying that it was the last question, but I forgot two or three very important questions, while we still have Exhibit 14.2 in front of the witness. Shall we continue with this now, or shall we leave it for tomorrow? I am at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is time for us to adjourn. We will resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 4.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
